titleStmt.title: Excavated texts 简牍 · 秦庄襄王元年: introductions

div.p: The entry for 249 BC in the Chronicle of the Shuihudi slips: the year alone, with nothing recorded under it.

A statute of the Yuelu Academy slips (volume IV, slips 329–331; the numbers in the text are the editors' slip numbers, register number and sequence number) from the reign of King Zhuangxiang: the Clerk of the Capital's report on the poor convict labour at the Western Workshop and the ruling on it.

The entry for the first year of King Zhuangxiang in the Suiji (Annual Record) of the Western Han slips from Hujiacaochang, Jingzhou, which names him by his later title and sums up his reign under its first year.

A persuasion on a wooden tablet (觚) from tomb M274 at Zhengjiahu, Yunmeng, Hubei, inscribed in seven lines on the front and six on the back and published in Wenwu 2022/3: a persuader named Tu urges a King of Qin to lay down arms, and is twice met with silence. The text, unknown to the received literature, names neither the king nor the year; the excavation report takes the king to be King Zhuangxiang and the occasion the five-state alliance of 247 BC. It is placed here with the appended texts of the Warring States persuaders.
